idiom_name: request value (receiver + parameters) + invoker/history + optional execute/undo pair
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define one request abstraction with a single execution operation - plus an inverse operation when undo is required - one concrete request per action holding a reference to its receiver and the parameters captured at creation time, and one invoker that stores, queues, schedules and logs requests without knowing their concrete type. The client is the only place that constructs and binds requests. Composite requests hold children so a group executes and undoes as one history entry. Where the language has first-class functions or closures, the concrete request usually collapses into a function value and only the invoker, the history and the inverse remain.
code_sketch:
command = bind(receiver, operation, parameters)   # client creates the request
invoker.history.append(command)                     # stored/logged, not yet run
invoker.execute(command)                            # later, possibly elsewhere
invoker.undo_last()                                 # command.undo() in reverse order
pitfalls: Letting the invoker construct or inspect concrete request types rebuilds the coupling the pattern removes, just at the other end.
Requests that capture live mutable receivers and run much later (queues, replay) apply a decision made against state that has since changed.
An unbounded history that never expires pins receivers and payloads - memory growth plus sensitive data persisted in logs.

Wrong move: push one command per keystroke or per drag frame with no merging -> the history explodes in memory and undo steps back a single character at a time -> instead: coalesce same-kind consecutive edits into one logical command (mergeWith()/id() in Qt, idempotent macro sealing on pause or focus change).

Wrong move: share one global command stack across multiple documents or editors -> undo reverts the wrong document when focus changes and macros interleave unrelated edits -> instead: keep one stack per document and route the UI through the active stack (QUndoGroup-style).

Wrong move: hand-roll command classes for plain deferred execution in a language with closures -> a type per action duplicates what a lambda or delegate already provides and every new action is a new file -> instead: pass a function value; promote to a command object only when undo, history, serialisation or queueing actually arrives.
